Integration guide — hand this to your coding agent INTEGRATION.md

Aegis mascot, widgets and sounds — integration brief

Audience: the coding agent integrating this kit into the Aegis voice-agent desktop app (Electron). This file is the single source of instructions. MASCOT.md and SOUNDS.md are reference catalogues; manifest.json is the same data in machine-readable form.

1. What you are integrating

PiecePurposeEntry point
The crew7 mascots, one per job (see section 2a): Aegi + mail, WhatsApp/socials, files, memory, harness, security. Each has its own shape, colours, personality and signature animationsCHARACTERS in src/mascot.js, character option everywhere
Mascot engineAnimated character showing what the agent is doing (34 states)src/mascot.js → AegisMascot, renderSVG, renderTrayIcon
Sounds17 interface sounds, synthesised at runtime (no audio files needed)src/sounds.js → AegisSounds
Event mapApp event → mascot state + soundsrc/events.js → EVENTS, STATE_SOUNDS
WidgetsReady-made desktop layouts that contain the mascotsrc/widgets.js → mountWidget, toast, linkWidgets
Tray iconsPer-state icons for the Windows system traytray/ico/<character>/<variant>/<state>.ico, tray/png/<character>/<variant>/<state>-<size>.png (size 16, 24, 32, 48), tray/svg/...
Static assetsAnimated + still SVG of every character, variant and statesvg/animated/<character>/<variant>/<state>.svg, svg/static/<character>/<variant>/<state>.svg (variant = color, dark, light)
Reference appTray + flyout + desktop pet + pill, wired over IPCelectron-example/

Everything in src/ is dependency-free ES modules. Install with npm install ./mascot-kit (package name aegis-mascot) or copy src/ into the renderer.

Verification status. The mascot engine, the widgets and both demo pages were exercised in headless Chromium with no errors. The Electron example was not run (Electron was not available where it was written): treat electron-example/ as a reference implementation to adapt and test, not as proven code. The sounds were checked numerically but not listened to.

2. The model: one state machine, many surfaces

The app has exactly one "agent state" at a time. Every surface (tray icon, flyout, desktop pet, pill, task card, toasts) renders that same state.

voice pipeline (main process)
        │  aegis.emit('mic:start')            aegis.update({ steps, progress })      aegis.say('agent', text)
        ▼
   IPC broadcast  ──►  every widget window  ──►  widget.emit(name) / widget.update(patch) / widget.say(role, text)
        ▲                                                │
        └──────────  'aegis:action' (mic, send, pause, resume, cancel, mute, close)  ◄── user clicks

Rules:

  1. The pipeline is the only thing that decides the state. Widgets never change state on their own in response to a click; they report the action and wait for the pipeline to emit the resulting event.
  2. Emit events ('prompt:send'), not raw states, so the sound and the mascot stay paired. Use setState only for states with no event.
  3. Exactly one renderer window owns an AegisSounds instance. Otherwise every window plays every sound.

Rules for the app:

  • Show Aegi while the user talks to the assistant and while it plans. When the pipeline routes work to a tool family, switch to that specialist and switch back to Aegi for the spoken answer.
  • Switch with a crew event (section 4, e.g. mail:new, harness:run, back with crew:lead) or directly: mascot.setCharacter('mail') / widget.setCharacter('mail'). The body morphs; colours and details change.
  • Map your tool names to characters in one place (suggested: email/calendar-mail tools → mail; WhatsApp, Telegram, Slack, X, Instagram → social; filesystem, drive, documents → files; memory / notes / RAG → memory; shell, code, MCP tools, tests, builds → harness; permission prompts, secrets, scans → security).
  • Every character plays all 16 common states. Signature states belong to one character; asking another character for them is allowed but the props are designed for the owner.
  • Each character has three variants: theme: 'color' (its own colour, default), 'dark', 'light'. Do not recolour a character with another character's colour: colour is how users tell them apart.

Events with a character in the table also switch the mascot to that crew member.

Typical run: mic:start → mic:stop → prompt:send → agent:searching / agent:working → agent:reply → agent:done → app:idle. Add or rename events by passing your own map: mountWidget(el, kind, { events }) / createAegis(el, { events }).

Screens: preview/widgets-light.png, preview/widgets-dark.png. Live: open demo/widgets.html and press "Run voice flow".

Options

mountWidget('#root', 'panel', {
  character: 'aegi',        // crew member: aegi | mail | social | files | memory | harness | security
  theme: 'color',           // 'color' (the character's own colour) | 'dark' | 'light' | custom theme object (see MASCOT.md)
  ui: 'light',              // 'light' | 'dark'  — widget chrome
  shape: null,              // optional body-shape override; leave unset to use the character's own shape
  size: 70,                 // mascot size in px (defaults per kind)
  state: 'idle',            // initial state
  sounds: sfx,              // an AegisSounds instance — pass it to ONE widget only
  follow: false,            // eyes follow the cursor (pet)
  title: 'Aegis', placeholder: 'Ask Aegis…',   // panel text
  timeout: 5000,            // toast auto-dismiss in ms (0 = stay)
  events: EVENTS,           // custom event map
});

Controller

CallEffect
w.emit('agent:done')Apply an event: mascot state + sound + default status text
w.setState('searching', { silent, then })Set a state directly
w.update({ status, sub, progress, steps, transcript })Set texts and data. progress: 0..1, or null for indeterminate. steps: `[{ label, state: 'todo''active''done' }]. transcript: [{ role: 'user''agent', text }]`
w.say(role, text)Append one transcript line (the pet and toast show it in the bubble)
w.on(action, fn)User actions: 'mic', 'send' (data = text), 'pause', 'resume', 'cancel', 'mute' (data = muted), 'close'; '*' for all
w.setCharacter('mail')Switch crew member
w.setTheme(theme), w.setUI('dark')Restyle
w.mascotThe underlying AegisMascot
w.destroy()Remove

linkWidgets([a, b, c]) returns a hub with the same methods that drives several widgets in one document at once (used by the demo). Across Electron windows, use IPC instead (section 6).

toast(target, { state: 'done', status: 'Task finished', sub: 'Report saved', theme, ui, sounds, timeout }) shows a toast.

All user-supplied text is inserted escaped. Status colours per state are in STATUS_COLORS; default status lines are in STATUS_TEXT (both exported, both in manifest.json).

6. Electron wiring

Reference: electron-example/main.js, preload.js, renderer.html.

Windows. One BrowserWindow per widget, all loading the same renderer.html?kind=<kind>&sounds=<0|1>.

WindowKey BrowserWindow options
allframe: false, transparent: true, resizable: false, skipTaskbar: true, hasShadow: false, webPreferences: { preload, contextIsolation: true, nodeIntegration: false, backgroundThrottling: false, autoplayPolicy: 'no-user-gesture-required' }
pet, pillalwaysOnTop: true, focusable: false; show with showInactive() so they never steal focus from the user's app
panelpositioned from tray.getBounds() + screen.getDisplayMatching(...).workArea; hide() on blur

IPC contract.

DirectionChannelPayload
main → rendereraegis:eventevent name (string)
main → rendereraegis:update{ status?, sub?, progress?, steps?, transcript? }
main → rendereraegis:sayrole, text
renderer → mainaegis:actionaction, data
renderer → mainaegis:hoverboolean — pointer is over the widget (for click-through)

Main-process API to expose to the pipeline (already in the example): aegis.emit(name), aegis.update(patch), aegis.say(role, text), aegis.onAction(fn).

Tray. On every event, map event → state and call tray.setImage(...) with tray/ico/<character>/<variant>/<state>.ico on Windows (tray/png/<character>/<variant>/<state>-32.png elsewhere) plus tray.setToolTip(...). Use variant color or light on light taskbars and dark on dark ones.shouldUseDarkColors`. Left click toggles the flyout; the context menu toggles pet and pill and offers Sleep and Quit.

Click-through. Transparent windows block clicks on the desktop under them. The example sends aegis:hover on mouseenter/mouseleave of the widget and the main process calls win.setIgnoreMouseEvents(!over, { forward: true }).

Dragging the pet. The mascot area has -webkit-app-region: drag. A drag region swallows click events, so if you need both drag and click-to-talk, implement dragging manually (pointer events → win.setPosition) instead. Persist the position.

Packaging. The example imports ../src/index.js directly. In a bundled app import from aegis-mascot; make sure tray/ is copied to resources (extraResources in electron-builder) because tray icons are loaded by path from the main process.

import { AegisSounds } from 'aegis-mascot';
const sfx = new AegisSounds({ pack: 'warm', volume: 0.6 });   // packs: `warm`, `crystal`
sfx.preload(); sfx.play('send'); sfx.startLoop('thinking-loop'); sfx.stopLoop('thinking-loop'); sfx.enabled = false;

Voice-specific rules:

  • Play listen-start before opening the microphone (wait ~450 ms or use echo cancellation) so speech-to-text does not transcribe the chime.
  • Do not play interface sounds while text-to-speech is talking; receive just before speech starts is enough.
  • tap is for Enter and button presses only, never per keystroke.
  • Expose mute and volume in settings (sfx.enabled, sfx.setVolume(v), sfx.setPack(name)).
  • Pre-rendered files exist in sounds/<pack>/<name>.wav|.mp3 if you prefer <audio> or a native player.

8. Mascot only (no widget)

import { AegisMascot, renderSVG, renderTrayIcon } from 'aegis-mascot';
const m = new AegisMascot('#slot', { character: 'aegi', theme: 'color', size: 120, follow: true, emblem: true, shadow: true });
m.setCharacter('mail'); m.setState('mail-incoming'); m.setCharacter('aegi'); m.setState('thinking');
m.setTheme('dark'); m.setTheme({ body: ['#FF7A59', '#7C3AED'], eye: '#fff', accent: '#111827', onAccent: '#fff', blush: '#FDBA74' });
const svg = renderSVG({ character: 'files', state: 'files-found', theme: 'color', animated: true });     // string, self-animating
const icon = renderTrayIcon({ character: 'aegi', state: 'listening', theme: 'dark' });            // string, square, readable at 16px

Variants per character: color, dark, light. Extra themes that work on any character: snow, aurora, sunset, ocean, candy, neon. Shape overrides: aegi, mail, social, files, memory, harness, security, leaf, orb, squircle, blob, drop, aegis. For small sizes (under ~64 px) pass emblem: false — the widgets already do this for pill, panel and toast.

9. Integration steps

  1. Add the package (npm install ./mascot-kit) and confirm demo/index.html (playground with all mascots) and demo/widgets.html (desktop widgets) both animate.
  2. Create the main-process aegis module (copy from electron-example/main.js): windows, tray, IPC, emit/update/say/onAction.
  3. Create the shared renderer page and preload (copy from the example). Give sounds=1 to exactly one window.
  4. Hook the voice pipeline: emit the events in section 4 at the matching points (mic open/close, prompt submitted, tool start, first reply token or TTS start, completion, error, cancel, pause/resume).
  5. Feed data: aegis.say() for transcript lines, aegis.update({ steps, progress, sub }) during tasks.
  6. Handle actions in the pipeline: mic (start listening), send (submit text), pause / resume, cancel, mute.
  7. Add settings: mascot theme, light/dark chrome (default: follow the OS), which widgets are visible, sound pack, volume, mute, do-not-disturb (app:sleep).
  8. Persist window positions and widget visibility; restore on launch; start with app:start.

10. Acceptance checklist

  • Every pipeline transition produces exactly one event; mascot state, tray icon and status text always agree across all windows.
  • Each sound plays once per event (not once per window) and never while the microphone is open.
  • Pause, resume and cancel from any widget reach the pipeline, and the UI changes only after the pipeline emits the resulting event.
  • Pet and pill never take keyboard focus; clicks outside the widget shape reach the desktop.
  • The flyout opens above the tray icon on any taskbar position and closes on blur or Escape.
  • Tray icon is legible on light and dark taskbars; tooltip names the current state.
  • One-shot states (hello, sending, cancelled, done) return to the right follow-up state.
  • With OS "reduce motion" on, the mascot shows still poses; with sounds muted, nothing plays.
  • Long transcripts scroll; long status text truncates without resizing the window.
  • No errors in any renderer console during a full run.

11. Regenerating assets

node tools/docs.mjs      # MASCOT.md, SOUNDS.md, INTEGRATION.md  (run first: the demo embeds them)
npm run build            # svg/, tray/svg/, sounds/*.wav, manifest.json, demo/*.html, preview/*.svg
python3 tools/tray.py    # tray/png + tray/ico   (pip install resvg-py pillow)

To add a character, theme, state, sound or event, edit CHARACTERS / THEMES / STATES in src/mascot.js, SOUNDS in src/sounds.js, or EVENTS in src/events.js, then rebuild. To edit this brief, change tools/INTEGRATION.template.md.

Mascot guide — the crew, states and files MASCOT.md

Aegi and the crew — the Aegis mascots

7 mascots, one per job. Aegi is the lead assistant; six specialists take over when their kind of work starts. They share one face (two oval eyes and a small mouth) so they read as one family, but each has its own body shape, colour, body details, idle personality and three signature animations. Original designs; the "one shape that morphs between states" idea is inspired by bloub.

The same states on every crew member:

Notes

  • "once" states (hello, sending, cancelled, done) play one time in the live component and then fall through to the next state. The exported SVG files of those states simply loop.
  • Every state starts and ends on the same pose, so the files loop without a jump.
  • In working, Aegi rolls into a ball; the specialists keep their shape.
  • Typical flow: listening → sending → thinking → (specialist takes over with a signature state) → speaking → done → idle.

Colours

Each character has three variants: color (its own colour), dark (dark body, bright outline in its colour) and light (cream body, outline in its colour).

The hues are spread around the colour wheel (terracotta, blue, green, amber, violet, teal, navy) so the crew members are easy to tell apart, and each keeps one small highlight colour. Extra themes that can be applied to any character: snow, aurora, sunset, ocean, candy, neon.

What is in this folder

PathWhat it is
svg/animated/<character>/<variant>/<state>.svgSelf-animating SVGs (loop forever, no JavaScript). Use in <img>, CSS backgrounds, README files.
svg/static/<character>/<variant>/<state>.svgStill frame of every state (icons, fallbacks, reduced-motion).
src/mascot.jsThe live engine: smooth morphing between states and characters, custom colours, cursor-following eyes. Zero dependencies.
src/index.jsMascot + sounds + widgets + the event map in one import.
src/widgets.jsDesktop widgets that contain the mascot: pill, desktop pet, tray flyout panel, task card, toast.
tray/System-tray icons per character, variant and state (SVG, PNG 16–48, ICO).
INTEGRATION.mdThe brief to hand to a coding agent: crew routing, widgets, Electron wiring, IPC contract, checklist.
demo/index.htmlThe playground: pick a mascot, try every state, colour, sound and event. The three guides are at the bottom of the page.
demo/widgets.htmlThe desktop-widget preview.
electron-example/Electron shell: tray icon + flyout + desktop pet + pill, driven over IPC (not run here — reference code).
manifest.jsonMachine-readable list of characters, states, sounds and events.
preview/Contact sheets.

Character = aegi, mail, social, files, memory, harness, security; variant = color, dark, light; state = any common state, plus that character's signature states.

Custom colours and new characters

Any colour can be a hex string or an array of gradient stops:

import { AegisMascot, renderSVG } from 'aegis-mascot';

const mine = { body: ['#FF7A59', '#7C3AED'], eye: '#FFFFFF', accent: '#111827', onAccent: '#FFFFFF', blush: '#FDBA74' };
new AegisMascot('#mascot', { character: 'memory', theme: mine, size: 160 });
fs.writeFileSync('thinking.svg', renderSVG({ character: 'memory', state: 'thinking', theme: mine }));   // Node: write your own file

To add a crew member: add a body outline to SHAPES, an entry to CHARACTERS (name, role, shape, face offset, palette, idle life), a body detail to FEATURE inside markup(), signature states to STATES with for: '<id>', events to src/events.js, then run npm run build.

Options: emblem (the body details / logo "A", default on; turn off below ~64 px), shadow (ground shadow, default on), shape (override the body with one of aegi, mail, social, files, memory, harness, security, leaf, orb, squircle, blob, drop).

Using it

1. Just the files (simplest — works anywhere):

<img src="svg/animated/aegi/color/thinking.svg" width="120" alt="Aegi is thinking">
<img src="svg/animated/mail/color/mail-incoming.svg" width="120" alt="New mail">

2. Live component (morphs between states):

import { AegisMascot } from 'aegis-mascot';
const aegi = new AegisMascot('#mascot', { character: 'aegi', theme: 'color', size: 160, follow: true });
aegi.setState('listening');
aegi.setCharacter('files'); aegi.setState('files-found');   // hand over to a specialist
aegi.setCharacter('aegi');
aegi.setState('sending', { then: 'searching' });   // one-shot, then continue somewhere specific
aegi.setTheme('dark'); aegi.setSize(96);
aegi.pause(); aegi.play(); aegi.destroy();

3. Custom element

<script type="module">import { defineElement } from 'aegis-mascot'; defineElement();</script>
<aegis-mascot character="harness" state="harness-running" theme="dark" size="120" follow></aegis-mascot>
<aegis-mascot state="idle" body="#22c55e" eye="#ffffff" accent="#052e16"></aegis-mascot>

4. Mascot + sounds from app events (recommended for the voice agent):

import { createAegis } from 'aegis-mascot';
const aegi = createAegis('#mascot', { character: 'aegi', size: 160, sounds: { pack: 'warm', volume: 0.6 } });
aegi.emit('mic:start');     // listening + "listen-start" sound
aegi.emit('prompt:send');   // sending   + "send"
aegi.emit('agent:done');    // done      + "done"
aegi.emit('user:cancel');   // cancelled + "cancel"
aegi.emit('mail:new');      // switches to Posty, plays mail-incoming + "notify"
aegi.emit('crew:lead');     // back to Aegi

The event → state → sound map is EVENTS in src/events.js; pass your own with createAegis(el, { events }).

Widgets and tray

mountWidget(target, 'pill' | 'pet' | 'panel' | 'card' | 'toast', opts) gives you the mascot inside a ready-made layout, and tray/ holds a per-state icon for the system tray. The full specification — sizes, window flags, IPC, checklist — is in INTEGRATION.md.

Electron

Install as a local package: npm install ./mascot-kit (or copy src/ into your renderer). It is plain ES modules with no dependencies, so it works with Vite, webpack, or directly with <script type="module">.

electron-example/ is a tray app with a flyout, a desktop pet and a pill. It has not been run in this workspace — Electron is not installed here — so treat it as reference code. See INTEGRATION.md section 6.

Good to know

  • Animated files use SVG SMIL animation: supported in Chromium/Electron, Firefox and Safari. Checked here in headless Chromium.
  • The live component respects prefers-reduced-motion (shows the still pose). For files, swap to svg/static/.
  • Animated files average ~25 KB.
  • Regenerate everything: npm run build (SVGs, sounds, demo, manifest) and node tools/docs.mjs (these docs).
Sounds guide SOUNDS.md

Aegis sound set

17 short interface sounds for the Aegis voice agent, in 2 packs. They are synthesised from code in src/sounds.js (no samples), so they are original and free to ship. Everything is tuned to one key (D major pentatonic), which is why any two of them sound right next to each other.

Honest note: these were generated and checked numerically (levels, lengths, clean endings) but not auditioned by ear — listen to them in demo/index.html and tell me which ones to retune.

Files

sounds/<pack>/<name>.wav (44.1 kHz, 16-bit mono) and sounds/<pack>/<name>.mp3.

PackCharacter
warmWarm (soft mallets)
crystalCrystal (glassy bells)

Which sound for which moment

Sound (file)Use it whenLengthApp events
tap — Key tapEnter key pressed, button pressed, any small click0.12skey:enter, social:react, harness:run
send — SendPrompt sent (Enter / send button)0.5sprompt:send, mail:send
send-soft — Send (alt, softer)Alternative send sound — quieter, for frequent sends0.5sfiles:upload, memory:save
receive — Message receivedAgent reply arrives / first token0.5sagent:reply, social:message, memory:recall
listen-start — Listening onMic opens / wake word detected0.45smic:start
listen-stop — Listening offMic closes / end of speech detected0.45smic:stop
pause — PauseUser pauses the agent / playback0.6suser:pause
resume — ResumeUser resumes after a pause0.6suser:resume
cancel — CancelUser cancels / stops the task0.45suser:cancel
done — DoneTask finished — the main "work is done" alert1.3sagent:done, files:found, security:locked
notify — NotificationReminder, incoming notification, needs attention1.1snotify, mail:new
error — ErrorSomething failed0.6sagent:error, security:alert
confused — ConfusedDidn't understand — ask the user to repeat0.65sagent:confused
wake — Wake / startupApp launch, agent comes online1.5sapp:start, crew:lead
sleep — Sleep / shutdownAgent goes idle, do-not-disturb on, app closing1.3sapp:sleep
celebrate — CelebrateBig success, milestone1.6sagent:celebrate
thinking-loop — Thinking (loop)Optional quiet bed while the agent works — loops seamlessly2s (loops)—

The ones you asked for

You asked forSoundMascot state
Pressing Entertap—
Sending a promptsend (or the quieter send-soft)sending
Pausepause (and resume to come back)paused
Cancelcancelcancelled
Work is donedonedone
Notification / alertnotifynotification

Extras for a voice agent: listen-start / listen-stop (mic open / closed), receive, confused, error, wake, sleep, celebrate, and thinking-loop (an optional quiet bed while the agent works).

Using them

Option A — no audio files at all (recommended in Electron; sounds are rendered on first use and cached):

import { AegisSounds } from 'aegis-mascot';
const sfx = new AegisSounds({ pack: 'warm', volume: 0.6 });
sfx.preload();                 // optional: render everything up front
sfx.play('send');
sfx.play('done', { volume: 0.8 });
sfx.startLoop('thinking-loop'); sfx.stopLoop('thinking-loop');
sfx.setPack('crystal'); sfx.setVolume(0.4); sfx.enabled = false;   // mute

Option B — the files:

const play = name => new Audio(`sounds/warm/${name}.mp3`).play();
play('cancel');

Option C — together with the mascot: createAegis(...).emit('prompt:send') — see MASCOT.md.

Voice-agent tips

  • Do not play sounds into an open microphone. Play listen-start *before* opening the mic (or enable echo cancellation), otherwise your speech-to-text will hear the chime.
  • Lower or mute interface sounds while text-to-speech is talking; receive right before speech starts is enough.
  • Browsers block audio until the first click or key press. In Electron set webPreferences.autoplayPolicy: 'no-user-gesture-required' (the example does).
  • Keep tap quiet and do not play it on every keystroke — only on Enter / button presses.
  • Give users a mute switch and a volume slider (sfx.enabled, sfx.setVolume).

Changing or adding sounds

Each sound is a few lines in SOUNDS in src/sounds.js (notes, timing, timbre). Edit, then npm run build to rewrite the WAV files. MP3s are made from the WAVs with ffmpeg: ffmpeg -i in.wav -codec:a libmp3lame -q:a 3 out.mp3.

If you want recorded sounds instead

Free libraries worth a look (check the licence on each official page before shipping):

  • Kenney — Interface Sounds: 100 clicks and feedback sounds, CC0, no attribution required.
  • soundcn: an open-source registry of 700+ CC0 interface sounds, installable per sound with the shadcn CLI.
  • Mixkit: notifications and transitions under its own free licence.
  • Freesound: huge, but the licence varies per sound — avoid anything marked non-commercial.
